If 'wansho' means 'Builder', why did Agelmar call Loial "Loial Kiseran" ("Glorious Loial") rather than "Loial Wansho" ("Builder Loial")? Loial is called Builder, I believe, in that same passage. So 'wansho' means 'glory' (though a distinct form of glory from 'daishar', battle blood). [[User:Dhasenan|Dhasenan]] 13:19, 1 August 2007 (UTC)

if 'Siswai' means spear what does 'darei' mean? it can't be a woman's spear because there is a society named Cor Darei meaning night spears. perhaps it is the differences between a personal spear and the spear of the public

I don't see much use for "public" spears versus "private" ones. It's probably a different type of spear, such as a naginata; or simply a different level of formality. [[User:Dhasenan|Dhasenan]] 22:30, 21 September 2008 (UTC)

== Another word ==

In Chapter 3, a Crown of Swords, the Wise One, Feraighin, calls Perrin "Sei'cair". [[User:Snadles|Snadles]] 05:51, July 22, 2010 (UTC)


It means "Goldeneyes". Sei == eye (seia doon "black eyes"; seiera "blue eyes" -- a type of flower; sei'mosiev "lowered eyes"); cair == golden (al'cair dal "the golden bowl"; a few others that I'm too lazy to go into). [[User:Dhasenan|Dhasenan]] 08:43, 22 July 2010 (UTC)
